Your records stay on this device, and this app never uploads them. Android backup may copy them if you have it switched on. The app uses the network only for the update check and for an update download, both started by you. Those two requests carry no ledger data and no identifier.
The full licence text of each component is available at its project page.
The first stable release. Identical to 0.1.0-rc.2 apart from this version string and this note.

A release tag with a suffix this build does not recognise is no longer dropped. It is read as a pre-release, so a new kind of tag can no longer hide a release from everyone. The home balance colours the whole line, label included.
The release candidate: the stable release with nothing changed but the version number. Everything else is the same.

Updates can now be downloaded and installed from inside the app. A downloaded file is checked against the SHA-256 published with the release, and only then handed to the system installer. Nothing is installed without your approval, and your records are not touched.
Long release histories no longer push the dialog buttons off the screen. Long button labels no longer break in half. The statistics date sits lower, with the period selector closer to it.

Buttons that belong in a dialog corner now sit there. A beta build can add the alpha releases to its history. The licence window keeps only what matters. The components and their links have a page of their own. The jump-to-today line no longer moves the statistics screen.
The version row now says what this build changed, and the update history is one button away. A stable build that is behind a beta is offered a way onto the test line from the update window.

A damaged or older database can no longer lock you out. The entry form keeps what you typed through a rotation or a theme change. The first frame no longer shows a balance of zero. Dark mode no longer opens with a white flash. An oversized import can no longer exhaust the memory available.

First beta. Preference reads and writes can no longer take the app down. A failed delete says so instead of crashing. An export is taken in one piece. The hot queries were checked against the database indexes.
A quick flick no longer deletes without a buzz. The statistics date stops moving when the jump-to-today line appears. The language list is ordered by language code, so Chinese no longer comes first.
Fixes the swipe-to-delete that had stopped working. A swipe that has gone far enough still buzzes. The rightward swipe on a row is gone. It never felt the same as swiping the page.

The balance is green in surplus and red in debt. A delete swipe now has to be deliberate, and it buzzes when it is. Swiping a row right turns to Statistics. The statistics date offers a way back to today.
Fixes the category buttons that could disappear from the entry form. The currency picker now offers nine signs on their own, with no currency names beside them.

Fixed several problems that showed up in daily use. The newest entry is no longer hidden behind the add button, and the keyboard no longer covers the save action. The form works again when every category has been deleted. Dates and clock times follow your language. Counted text uses proper plural forms. A damaged settings file no longer stops the app from starting.

The statistics breakdown now splits each category by the direction its transactions were recorded with. Changing a category type no longer moves money to the other side of the screen, and the donut no longer disagrees with the totals above it.

Amounts typed on a comma keyboard are read correctly, not multiplied by a hundred. A backup carrying no records is refused instead of erasing the ledger. The update dialog shows release notes as text, not Markdown.

The update check falls back to the GitHub release feed when the API refuses or cannot be read. Each failure now gets its own message instead of one sentence for all of them. It also waits longer on a slow connection.
First published build. Manual entry with categories and notes. The month view groups by day. Statistics cover year, month and day. Nine languages and JSON backup.
